summary: I read the Firefighter class (agents.py:379-1178) in full and mechanically extracted every model attribute it touches. The result is decisive: a Firefighter's entire interface to the world is four model attributes — `self.model.schedule` (to enumerate Fire agents), `self.model.grid`, `self.model.HEIGHT/WIDTH`, plus three write-only outbound channels (`_agents_pending_removal`, `_rescue_path_clear_requested`, `_on_firefighter_route_blocked`). Its behaviour is driven entirely by its own instance fields (`target_pos`, `exiting`, `exit_target`, `rescued_victim`, `dead`, `assigned`) and by live fire/smoke geometry read straight off the Fire agents; two module-level ints (IDLE_RETREAT_SAFETY_BUFFER=3, IDLE_RETREAT_MAX_CELLS=6 at agents.py:375-376) are read as globals, not through the model, so nothing can retune them at runtime either. `target_pos` — the single field that could carry a "go here" order — has exactly four writers repo-wide, and every one either nulls it or sets it to a *victim marker's own cell*. The global adaptation layer cannot reach any of this: MissionDecision has no firefighter field at all, and GlobalExecutor writes only `uav_resource_model`, `managed_uav_states`, `sop.mission_mode` and `pending_global_commands`. The rescue lane is a near-miss rather than a path: `RescueExecutor.execute()` — the *only* method the planning layer's RescueDecision actually reaches, via decision_dispatcher.py:121 — writes solely into knowledge mirrors and never touches a marker, while the method that does mutate markers (`apply_physical_pairing_decision`) is called only by wildfire_model, which re-derives the pairing itself from `select_rescue_assignment` and throws the planner's choice away. firefighter_state.py, firefighter_model.py and firefighter_monitor.py are pure read-only mirrors with no write-back function of any kind. Answer to Q5: there is no path today, not even a broken one — the destination field to write does not exist.

blockers.name: MissionDecision has no firefighter channel — every field is UAV-keyed
blockers.evidence: The full field list is: `uav_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `task_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `mission_mode: str`, `relay_assignments: dict[str, str]`, `recall_orders: tuple[str, ...]`, plus confidence/uncertainty/comparison/explanation/selected_option_id/notes. The global layer's output type literally has nowhere to put a firefighter order, so the break is upstream of any plumbing question — even a perfectly wired executor would have nothing to read. This is the root break: it is why the background arming experiment that populated `uav_assignments` as a proper dict changed outcomes while the fire map stayed byte-identical — the only thing a MissionDecision can move is UAVs.

notes:
PLAIN ANSWER TO Q5: No. If the global layer wanted to hand a firefighter a region to defend or a fire-front sector, there is no path today — and the gap is not one broken link but a missing destination. Four breaks, in order of depth: (1) MissionDecision has no firefighter field, so the order cannot even be expressed; (2) GlobalExecutor has no firefighter sink, so it could not be carried; (3) the Firefighter agent reads no model attribute that src_extension writes, so it could not be received; (4) `target_pos` is a single cell forced to equal a victim marker's position, so "region" and "sector" have no representation at all. Fixing any one of these alone changes nothing.

THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND *NOT* BROKEN — there IS one real, live write path from src_extension into firefighter behaviour, and I want to be precise that it exists rather than overstate the isolation: rescue_executor.py:248 `applied = bool(apply_cmd(command))` calls `model.apply_physical_rescue_command`, which at wildfire_model.py:3498-3503 really does set `assigned`, `target_pos`, `rescued_victim`, `status`, `exiting`, `exit_target`. That path works and moves real firefighters. But it is not an adaptation channel: it is a round-trip. wildfire_model calls out to the executor (`_execute_physical_rescue_via_executor`, :3042-3047) purely to get an audit trail and event recording, and the executor calls straight back into the model. Every one of the six call sites (wildfire_model.py:2829, 2870, 2894, 3787, 3811, 3989, 4203) originates in wildfire_model from physics events — victim confirmed, route blocked, firefighter casualty, rescue complete — never from a trigger, an option, or a decision. src_extension supplies the authority wrapper, not the intent.

Also worth flagging as a genuine near-miss rather than a dead end: the adaptation layer DOES generate firefighter-shaped options today. rescue_adaptation_generator.py:347 emits `option_id="rescue_firefighter_assignment_nearest"` with `assignment_action: "assign_nearest_firefighter"`, and RescuePlanner.plan() (rescue_planner.py:64-130) scores them and emits a RescueDecision carrying a `firefighter_id`. So intent is produced — it just terminates in the knowledge mirror. Of everything traced, this is the shortest fix: `RescueExecutor.execute()` already receives that decision and already has `model` in hand; routing an "assign" action through `apply_physical_pairing_decision` (which sits 200 lines below it in the same class) would connect the planner to real dispatch. That would let the global layer choose WHICH firefighter goes to WHICH victim. It still would not deliver a defend-region order — that needs a new field, per blocker 5.

One correction to a natural assumption: `_check_rescue_assignment_invariant` in adaptation_manager.py:224 and `_process_rescue_incidents` at :342 look like adaptation-layer control over rescue, but neither is. The first is explicitly "Log firefighter/victim assignment divergence. Does not repair state." The second just drains a model-owned queue via `_call_stage(model, "_process_rescue_incidents")` and counts what passed through — the queue's contents and all decision logic are model-side.

Finally, on indirect influence: I confirmed src_extension cannot steer firefighters through the fire either. Every reference to `is_burning` across the extension (uav_executor, environment_bridge, environment_monitor, local_uav_monitor, dashboard_state_builder) is a read; there are no writes to `.burning`, `.fuel`, `_rescue_path_clear_requested`, `_agents_pending_removal`, HEIGHT or WIDTH anywhere in src_extension. That is the structural reason behind the background finding that the fire map stayed byte-identical across all 13 arming runs.

notes:
Things I checked and found NOT broken, plus surprises:

(1) COMMUNICATION scope is the counter-example that proves the pattern is fixable, and it is the only scope that is essentially wired. communication_adaptation_generator.py:226-237 writes the evaluator's own key names directly into base_parameters:
            \"delivery_quality\": delivery_confidence,
            \"sync_quality\": float(comm_snapshot.get(\"sync_quality\", delivery_confidence) or delivery_confidence),
            \"critical_support\": 0.85 if rescue_active else 0.35,
plus \"delivery_confidence\" (:227, read at utility_evaluation.py:1212) and \"relay_cost\": 0.35 (:306). Coverage is 4/5 — only `delay_cost` (utility_evaluation.py:1210) has zero write-sites. So the comm evaluator does real work on real options. This is what a connected scope looks like, and it shows the disconnection is per-generator sloppiness rather than a missing architectural layer.

(2) There is no enrichment/adapter layer anywhere between generation and scoring, and I looked specifically for one. The only writes to option.parameters in all of src_extension are local_adaptation_generator.py:2463-2464 and :2499 (`sector_assigned`, `flank_split` — sector bookkeeping), and constraint_filter.py:231 is a read (`return option.parameters[key]`). fail_safe_planner.py:540 `params.update({...})` looked promising but is `_fallback_option_from_strategy` building a fallback plan option from a FallbackStrategy, writing fail_safe_action / mission_mode / target_entity / fallback_strategy / explanation / search_mode — none of the utility keys. So there is no half-built reducer to finish; the layer was never started.

(3) Docs describe the intended inputs for exactly one scope. docs/04_clean_separation_table.md enumerates ten runtime knowledge models (headers at :97 Fire Belief, :129 Visibility/Uncertainty, :156 Victim, :188 UAV Resource and Role, :222 Firefighter, :242 Communication, :263 Mission Goal, :280 Shared Operational Picture, :299 Local Observation, :315 Local Path Context). Only the last one lists utility-shaped fields. There is NO \"Global Mission Context Model\" and no global utility spec anywhere. docs/03_managing_system.md:79-89 is the only place the utility layer is described at all, and it is a bare bullet list — \"utility functions / option scoring / feasibility checks / threshold checks / ranking mechanisms\" — with no term names, no formula, no inputs. grep for all 9 keys across docs/*.md, src_extension/*.md (ARCHITECTURE_BOUNDARIES.md, MANAGING_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md, README_extension_structure.md) and README.md returns exactly one line, docs/04:323 `- local_collision_risk_estimates`, which belongs to the Local Path Context Model. Plainly: the 9 global keys are documented nowhere, under any name.

(4) Git history rules out a deleted producer. `git log --oneline -S'\"fire_contribution\"' --all` yields a single commit, a4a01b4 (2 commits deep in a 43-commit history), which added src_extension/planning/utility_evaluation.py (+1618) alongside tests/test_global_local_planners.py (+226) and the other utility tests in one shot. Scorer and synthetic tests were born together; no generator ever wrote these keys and none was removed.

(5) Why the do-nothing baseline is the only global option that scores. global_adaptation_generator.py:23-26 emits parameters `{\"stability_action\": \"maintain_current_config\", \"do_nothing\": True}`. `do_nothing` is precisely the flag `ptruth(\"stability_control\", \"do_nothing\")` at utility_evaluation.py:825 that sets is_stability_idle, which is the sole gate on the S_stability_idle_floor term at :907-909 (`idle_floor = 0.05 * profile.stability_weight if is_stability_idle else 0.0`). Combined with S_hysteresis_bonus (:892-901), that is the entire 0.153-0.255 you measured. The one option that wins is the one whose score is manufactured from two constants and the string \"do_nothing\".

(6) Grep hygiene warning for anyone re-running this. summary: I enumerated every test under tests/ that imports or exercises utility_evaluation, global_mission_planner, global_executor, global_adaptation_generator, decision_objects/MissionDecision, planning_coordinator, or decision_dispatcher (29 files by import; 3 more — test_adaptation_integration.py, test_planning_integration.py, test_execution_integration.py — exercise the real path without importing them), and read every assertion in them. The headline finding is that the suite does NOT lock the broken behaviour at the utility layer: every global-utility and global-planner test hand-writes the 9 keys into synthetic MissionAdaptationOption.parameters, so if the generator started emitting those keys, or the planner started selecting non-baseline options, ZERO existing assertions would break. Only ONE mechanical blocker exists for a MissionDecision field addition — an exact set-equality assertion at tests/test_planner_core.py:51 — plus a sibling at tests/test_utility_core.py:46 for OptionEvaluation. The real obstacles are design gaps in production code, not tests: the generator writes assigned_role as a bare string that _uav_assignments_from_params silently drops, and the role vocabulary it emits ("fire_tracking", "victim_search") does not match the runtime vocabulary ("fire_tracker", "victim_searcher") that the local path generator compares against with exact equality, so populating uav_assignments would write roles nothing downstream recognizes. No CI config, pytest.ini, tox.ini, or docs note about test counts exists anywhere in the repo; I corroborated the maintainer's 8-failed/427-passed baseline from .pytest_cache instead.
